bullets: Germanicus is stronger: Fight to the Death now gives +1 to EACH die when he is down to exactly 2 troops (was +1 to just the highest die). At 1 troop it is still +2 to the die roll.

Target-first attacks: click a province and choose "Attack here from ...", then pick one of your provinces that can legally attack it — the battle then plays exactly as if you had attacked from the Actions panel.
No more double popup for a drawn card: when you draw a card you now see it once, not twice.
Busy Little Bee! now waits: played on a "Rome is Displeased" roll, the penalty lands at the start of the targeted player's next turn instead of vanishing because it isn't their turn.
"You are attacked!" now shows the full battle details: who is attacking, which province is under attack, how many troops you have there, where your general is, and the cards played against you.
Mobile startup choices are now popup buttons: the AI skill choice and the General choice open a popup instead of cramped dropdowns.
New: this changelog — a "What's New" view on the startup page with the version history, newest first.
title: Germanicus buff, target-first attacks & more

bullets: Revolt! and a rival's Bribe the Ally! can no longer target a player with only 1 or 2 provinces.
Converting your own allied province with Bribe the Ally! is unchanged, and the Revolt Roll (the dice roll at the start of a turn) is unchanged.
title: Small-empire protection

bullets: The move counter (0/2, 1/2, 2/2) now sits right next to the "4. Actions" header.
Losing an allied province in battle no longer costs you prestige (the attacker still gains 1 for the conquest).
Placing survivors after a conquest is now one popup with a slider between the two provinces, showing each province's minimum garrison; whether the general goes back is a simple checkbox.
When it isn't your turn and you earn a Game Card, it is drawn automatically and shown to you — no Draw click needed.
title: Survivors slider, allied losses & auto-drawn cards

bullets: Online games now connect through Cloudflare relays, so joining from another network is more reliable.
note: Sourced from the v31.21.1 commit message on main, not from MUSE_CHANGES.md (which has no section for this patch version).
title: Online play: more reliable connections

bullets: Joining an online game is simpler: one Join screen covers a first join, joining mid-game, and coming back after dropping out — and the host picks your seat.
Rejoining a saved online game works more smoothly: the host keeps its connection across Resume.

The rules book is now the official rules file, rewritten and clarified — including that rolls of 2 and 9 are never Rome Rolls, and the five-general roster (Caesar, Scipio, Pompey, Germanicus and Augustus).
title: Simpler online joining & the official rules book

bullets: Connection relays for online play were restored, so a guest on another network can reach the host again.
note: Sourced from the v31.20.1 commit message on main, not from MUSE_CHANGES.md (which has no section for this patch version).
title: Online play: guests on another network can connect again

bullets: A Merchant ship must touch one of your own coastal provinces: you can't buy or move a ship on a sea link that doesn't touch your coast.
The rules text now matches how the game already plays, including the five-general roster and generals moving as many times as they want in a turn.
title: Merchant ships must touch your own coast

bullets: The Sneak Attack from the Sea! card now uses its own artwork instead of the generic card back.
Augustus's card and map token, and the merchant ship picture, now use their proper art instead of placeholders.
title: New artwork

bullets: A general leaving Roma can now go straight to any province you control — Roma escorts him, no link needed.
If your general wasn't on the board when he is recalled, he stays off the board instead of appearing in Roma.
The AI can now play Sneak Attack from the Sea! when the odds are good (it never could before).
Buying a ship is now a two-step pick: first your coastal province, then the sea-linked partner.
Rules wording: only a player-controlled Carthage satisfies the Senate on rolls of 2 and 9.
title: Roma escort, Sneak Attack AI & a two-step ship picker

bullets: Game Rolls of 2 and 9 now follow who controls Carthage: only a player currently holding Carthage satisfies the Senate — neutral or unowned Carthage still raises a Senate Decree.
Rolls of 1 and 10 are still Rome Rolls.
title: Game Rolls 2 and 9 follow who controls Carthage

bullets: A recalled general's token goes to Roma, all his perks switch off while he is recalled, and he can't move or join attacks until the recall ends — house arrest in Rome.
Your general can now move as many times as you want in a turn — still free, still not an action.
title: Recalled generals go to Roma & unlimited general moves

bullets: Merchant Bonus now starts at 2 Roads and pays Roads minus 1 (2 Roads = +1 Gold, 3 Roads = +2, and so on, with no cap).
A Merchant ship now costs 5 Gold (was 8).
The Bribe the Ally! text now correctly says converting your own ally gives +1 Prestige (the game already did).
title: Merchant Bonus starts at 2 Roads & cheaper ships

bullets: The AI now only fights on to burn your Elephants and Moral Boosts when it has enough troops elsewhere to afford the losses — with thin reserves it retreats as before.
title: Smarter AI elephant logic

bullets: New purchase: buy 1 Prestige for 20 Gold. Unlike standing Gold Prestige, bought prestige is banked permanently — it can't vanish if the gold is spent or taken.
The AI values allies more: it allies more often and holds on to Bribe the Ally! instead of selling it first.
The AI now sometimes fights on to burn your Elephants and Moral Boosts instead of retreating and handing them back.
The rules book now matches the game on Bribe the Ally! (+1 Prestige for converting your own ally) and the Merchant Bonus (Roads minus 2, no cap).
Fixed: playing Sneak Attack with no actions left could lock the game — the card now stays in your hand.
title: Buy Prestige for Gold & a smarter AI

bullets: Germanicus's perks are now described correctly in the rules (Fight to the Death: +1 to the highest die at 2 troops, +2 at 1).
The battle screen lists Fight to the Death up front, and no longer claims the Wall is ignored when there is no Wall.
Dice that a perk adjusted are now marked with a +N badge in the battle table.
The General button stays visible until End Turn (greyed with the reason when you can't move him).
Your general's token on the map is clickable — tap it to pick where he moves.
title: Germanicus battle display & a clickable general

bullets: New AI difficulty: the current AI is now "Normal", and there's a gentler "Easy" you can pick per AI seat at setup.
Easy AI never plays Revolt! or Assassin! against you in the first 10 rounds, then only half as often — and it attacks your provinces at most once per turn.
title: AI difficulty: Normal & Easy

bullets: New dice button next to the Seed field, and every new game now starts with a fresh random seed.
A played Sneak Attack card now goes to a throwaway pile for good — so it can happen at most twice per game.
Cards added to old saves (like Sneak Attack) now shuffle into the deck instead of landing at the bottom where you'd never draw them.
Revolt! and Bribe the Ally! now name the general when he is the reason a card can't be played.
title: Fresh seeds, a throwaway pile & clearer card messages

bullets: Revolt! now tells you when the general is the reason it can't be played, instead of only citing the troop rule.
Sneak Attack can now target coastal provinces whose natives haven't been rolled yet — their natives are rolled when you pick them.
The desktop Sneak Attack flow now has a "Review attack" button on the troop step, so it no longer dead-ends.
title: Sneak Attack fixes

bullets: Your general now protects the province he stands on: it can't Revolt or be bribed away by a rival (converting your own ally still works).
New Game Card: "Sneak Attack from the Sea!" (×2) — attack any coastal province from one of your coastal provinces with a Road.
title: Your general protects his province & Sneak Attack!
